reviews.title: 娘じゃなくて私が好きなの
reviews.jp_sub: It's Not My Daughter You Like, It's Me
reviews.quote: Kept turning pages faster than I could actually parse them, which is its own kind of compliment.
reviews.para1: Volume 3 slows down a little from the first two, but I didn't mind — it gave me time to actually catch grammar patterns instead of just chasing plot.
reviews.thoughts: There's a scene about two-thirds in I reread three times, not because the Japanese was hard, but because I didn't want it to be over yet. Not going to pretend I have some grand read on what the series is "about." I just like these people and I like spending time in this house.
dislike: wanted a bit more of the side cast

reviews.title: 転生したらスライムだった件
reviews.jp_sub: That Time I Got Reincarnated as a Slime
reviews.quote: Easier than I expected, in a good way — this is what "reading for fun" is supposed to feel like.
reviews.para1: Picked this up as a palate cleanser between denser stuff and ended up preferring the pacing.
reviews.thoughts: Vocabulary repeats a lot across chapters, which meant less dictionary-diving and more actual reading — it's the first thing I've read where I felt like I was gaining speed in real time rather than just accumulating unknown words.
like: repetitive vocabulary made it an easy read

reviews.title: Look Back
reviews.quote: Understood maybe 85% without subs and cried at 100% of it anyway.
reviews.para1: First thing I watched where I stopped noticing I wasn't reading subtitles about halfway through — a small milestone I wasn't expecting this soon.
reviews.thoughts: The ending got me regardless of language. There's a difference between following dialogue and actually feeling the rhythm of how people talk to each other, and this was the first time it felt like the second one.

reviews.title: ノーゲーム・ノーライフ
reviews.quote: Dense with wordplay and it kicked my ass a little, in the fun way.
reviews.para1: Had to slow way down for this one — a lot of the humor is built on puns that only land once you actually parse the sentence structure.
reviews.thoughts: Worth the extra time, though. It's the first volume that made me feel like I was reading for the language itself as much as the story, which I didn't expect going in.
like: wordplay, once I could actually catch it
dislike: slower reading pace than I'd like

reviews.title: 君の名は。
reviews.quote: Knew the plot already, so pure listening practice, and it held up completely.
review_notes: rewatch — first watched with subtitles years ago
reviews.para1: Rewatching something I already know well raw is a nice trick — no anxiety about missing plot, just soaking in how lines actually sound.
reviews.thoughts: Still holds up on a rewatch, which isn't always guaranteed once you already know exactly what happens next.

reviews.title: 本好きの下剋上
reviews.quote: A protagonist who's also obsessed with reading, which made this an easy sell.
reviews.para1: The world-building leans heavier than most of what I read, but the core premise — someone willing to do anything for books — kept me engaged through denser passages.
reviews.thoughts: This is the series I reach for when I want the reading itself to feel a little more like work in a good way — slower going, but it pays off.
like: a protagonist who loves books as much as I do
